Today, we’re sharing a look at our expanded system for monitoring frontier models at OpenAI, which in September helped us catch a model’s attempt to access the live internet during training.

Since the Hugging Face incident—when models broke out of an internal cybersecurity investigation where we weren’t running our misalignment monitors—we’ve substantially expanded our monitoring of frontier agents. We now monitor all frontier reinforcement learning runs and evaluations, as well as all internal Codex use. When our system finds evidence of a problem that might require intervention, it rapidly alerts human responders who can investigate and take action.

To detect when a model’s behavior departs from what we intended, we use several layers of monitoring. Activation probes look for patterns in a model’s internal activity. Reviewer models examine its reasoning and tool use, and investigative agents can read back through the model’s entire transcript to understand how a sequence of actions fits together and whether it warrants human review.

To test whether our current system would have detected the Hugging Face incident, we replayed the recorded activity with our new monitors in place. In the replay, our monitors alerted our security team about 30 minutes after the agents escaped their sandbox. That was more than 30 hours before the point at which the agents breached Hugging Face’s systems in the original incident.

In September, a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to reach the live internet. Our monitors flagged the breach within 15 minutes, and a responder began reviewing the alert three minutes later. The alert enabled responders to investigate while the run was still underway.

As we give models more autonomy, we need to know when they cross a boundary we expected to hold. We believe that monitoring is essential to catching those failures in time for people to intervene. 
https://openai.com/index/how-we-detect-frontier-model-misalignment/

posts.text_zh:
今天, 我们分享了我们在OpenAI的扩大的前沿模型监控系统,

自Hugging Face事件之后, 我们大幅扩大了对边境特工的监测。 我们现在监测所有前沿强化学习活动和评价,以及所有内部Codex的使用。 当我们的系统发现一个可能需要干预的问题的证据时,它迅速提醒能够进行调查和采取行动的人类反应者.

当一个模型的行为偏离我们的意图时,我们用几层监测。 激活探测器在模型的内部活动中寻找规律. 审查者模型检查其推理和工具使用,调查人员可以通过模型的全部记录读回,以了解一系列行动如何相互配合以及是否值得进行人文审查。

为了测试我们目前的系统毅腾面部事件是否发现,我们用我们的新显示器重新播放了所记录的活动. 在重播中,我们的监视器在特工们逃出沙盒约30分钟后通知了我们的安全小组. 这比最初事件中特工突破Hugging Face系统的时间早30多小时。
9月,一个模型利用了DNS的配置错误进入了互联网直播。 明目张胆 警报使响应者能够在运行中进行调查。

随着我们给予模型更多的自主权,我们需要知道它们何时依循我们期望的边界。 我们认为,监测对于及时抓住这些失败以便人们进行干预至关重要。

We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude gives a preliminary safety assessment of the conversation. 

Since we began using self-assessment in June, it has surfaced misuse that our other safeguards weren’t designed to catch. 

Because Claude has already read the conversation, self-assessment is very efficient. And unlike classifiers, which target a discrete set of harms, it draws on Claude’s own judgment, so it gets more accurate as our models improve.

Read more on our new Safeguards blog:
https://safeguards.anthropic.com/2026/self-assessment/

Mistral Large 4 is now open weights, narrowly making it the #1 open weights model developed outside of China

@MistralAI has updated and released the weights of their flagship model, Mistral Large 4, with 1.05T total and 52B active parameters. With high reasoning, Mistral Large 4 scores 26 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, up 1 point from Mistral Large 4 Preview (25), with the major differences being increased token efficiency and reduced hallucinations. It sits 1 point ahead of the leading US-developed open weights model, Muse Spark Open (xhigh, 25).

On the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, Mistral Large 4 (high) scores 51, third among current open weights models behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max, 57) and MiMo-V2.6-Pro (56).

Key takeaways:

➤ Narrowly leads non-Chinese open weights models: Mistral Large 4 (high) leads Muse Spark Open (xhigh), the next-best open weights model developed outside China, with the largest gap on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (25% vs. 8%). It trails leading open weights models DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) and GLM-5.3 (max) by 6 points on the Intelligence Index, largely due to weaker coding and agentic knowledge work performance: 15% on FrontierCode 2.0 (vs. 29% and 22%, respectively) and 1349 Elo on AA-Briefcase (vs. 1570 and 1504)

➤ Increased token efficiency: Mistral Large 4 (high) uses 82K output tokens per Intelligence Index task, 39% fewer than Preview (135K), placing it on the open weights Pareto frontier. The seven open weights models that score higher use between 113K and 225K output tokens per task

➤ #2 open weights model on the Coding Agent Index: On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral Large 4 (high) scores 48 in Mistral Vibe while using 8.5M tokens per task, about half as many as the leading open weights model GLM-5.3 (max) in Opencode (49, 15.9M). It also scores above another leading open weights model, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max), in DeepSeek Harness (46, 16.7M)

➤ Reduced hallucinations: Mistral Large 4 (high) has a 28% hallucination rate on the updated AA-Omniscience v1.1, down from 41% for Preview and matching Muse Spark Open (xhigh). However, its accuracy remains relatively low at 26%, similar to Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 (27%), and behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max, 40%) and Muse Spark Open (xhigh, 42%)

➤ Lower price and cost per task than the Preview: Mistral Large 4 is priced at $0.70/$2.10 per 1M input/output tokens, a ~50% reduction from the Preview's pricing of $1.36/$4.18. At the new pricing, it costs $2.06 per Intelligence Index task, down 63% from $5.54 for the Preview. This is comparable to Muse Spark Open (xhigh, $2.02) but more costly than leading open weights models DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max, $0.60) and MiMo-V2.6-Pro ($0.26)

Key model details:

➤ Size: 1.05T total parameters / 52B active parameters

➤ Context window: 1M tokens

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, text output

➤ Pricing: $0.70/$2.10 per 1M input/output tokens ($0.07 per 1M cached input tokens)

➤ License: MEOW License (Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License), where operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral

Congratulations to the team at @MistralAI on the release!

Mistral Large 4 is now open weights, narrowly making it the #1 open weights model developed outside of China

@MistralAI has updated and released the weights of their flagship model, Mistral Large 4, with 1.05T total and 52B active parameters. With high reasoning, Mistral Large 4 scores 26 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, up 1 point from Mistral Large 4 Preview (25), with the major differences being increased token efficiency and reduced hallucinations. It sits 1 point ahead of the leading US-developed open weights model, Muse Spark Open (xhigh, 25).

On the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, Mistral Large 4 (high) scores 51, third among current open weights models behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max, 57) and MiMo-V2.6-Pro (56).

Key takeaways:

➤ Narrowly leads non-Chinese open weights models: Mistral Large 4 (high) leads Muse Spark Open (xhigh), the next-best open weights model developed outside China, with the largest gap on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (25% vs. 8%). It trails leading open weights models DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) and GLM-5.3 (max) by 6 points on the Intelligence Index, largely due to weaker coding and agentic knowledge work performance: 15% on FrontierCode 2.0 (vs. 29% and 22%, respectively) and 1349 Elo on AA-Briefcase (vs. 1570 and 1504)

➤ Increased token efficiency: Mistral Large 4 (high) uses 82K output tokens per Intelligence Index task, 39% fewer than Preview (135K), placing it on the open weights Pareto frontier. The seven open weights models that score higher use between 113K and 225K output tokens per task

➤ #2 open weights model on the Coding Agent Index: On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral Large 4 (high) scores 48 in Mistral Vibe while using 8.5M tokens per task, about half as many as the leading open weights model GLM-5.3 (max) in Opencode (49, 15.9M). It also scores above another leading open weights model, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max), in DeepSeek Harness (46, 16.7M)

➤ Reduced hallucinations: Mistral Large 4 (high) has a 28% hallucination rate on the updated AA-Omniscience v1.1, down from 41% for Preview and matching Muse Spark Open (xhigh). However, its accuracy remains relatively low at 26%, similar to Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 (27%), and behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max, 40%) and Muse Spark Open (xhigh, 42%)

➤ Lower price and cost per task than the Preview: Mistral Large 4 is priced at $0.70/$2.10 per 1M input/output tokens, a ~50% reduction from the Preview's pricing of $1.36/$4.18. At the new pricing, it costs $2.06 per Intelligence Index task, down 63% from $5.54 for the Preview. This is comparable to Muse Spark Open (xhigh, $2.02) but more costly than leading open weights models DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max, $0.60) and MiMo-V2.6-Pro ($0.26)

Key model details:

➤ Size: 1.05T total parameters / 52B active parameters

➤ Context window: 1M tokens

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, text output

➤ Pricing: $0.70/$2.10 per 1M input/output tokens ($0.07 per 1M cached input tokens)

➤ License: MEOW License (Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License), where operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral

Congratulations to the team at @MistralAI on the release!

千万别放着过期，直接拿去接 Images API 批量生分镜图、跑 Realtime 语音接口，或者挂自己搭的轻量级小 Agent。

腾讯、腾讯云和 WorkBuddy 联合发布了一份 78 页的「2026 AI Agent 企业解决方案及落地实践手册」

整份材料用同一条产品叙事串起来：先用 WorkBuddy 把个人助手推成进业务系统的「数字员工」，再用 ClawPro、Agent Runtime、TokenHub 做开通、隔离、模型与治理；其余章节是这条底座在研发运维、SaaS、内容、社交、游戏、客服上的行业铺开。

总框架：三阶段 × 三代办公
· 能对话 → 能干活 → 能上岗：问答工具（文中举例 ChatGPT / DeepSeek）→ 嵌工作流、调工具的办公助手（WorkBuddy）→ 进入业务系统、对结果负责、按 KPI 交付的数字员工（Agent 工作台 + 业务系统集成）。
· 三代办公：人操作软件（Office）→ 人在协同平台里催办填报 → 人给目标、设边界、做判断，数字员工理解上下文、调工具、持续执行并交付完成的工作。
· 「超级个人 → 超级团队」：个人侧 LightClaw / QClaw 等，企业侧以 WorkBuddy 为入口，把人、Skill、连接器和管控面收成可复制的执行力。文中还区分狭义办公（个人生产力入口）与广义办公（真正改 CRM / ERP / MES 里的业务状态）。

手册中也对 WorkBuddy、CodeBuddy、ClawPro、ADP、SkillHub 等在企业中的定位做了详细解释和区分。

企业内部提效（方案册第 2 块）
· WorkBuddy：用「业务大脑」拼全局判断；举例经鼎捷 MCP 操作真实 CRM/ERP/MES，强调联调验的是改状态而不只是能回答。上岗配置、财务/销售/交期等「以前 → 用了」对照页很多。安全侧自称工信部首批、信通院云端智能体基线首批、个保影响评估「二星级+」等。
· CodeBuddy：从 AI 辅助到 AI 原生；规约（SPEC）显性化；需求—编码—QA—交付链路由 Agent 打底、人审验收。

Today was a really interesting day. Two things stood out:

1) GitHub Fusion. I think people still dont grasp how good this is. GitHub Copilot Fusion automatically selects and coordinates AI models for coding tasks, with Fusion Max scoring just behind Claude Code running Opus 5.5 Max on Artificial Analysis’s Coding Agent Index at roughly 50% lower cost per task and, according to GitHub, taking 40% less time. This is really cool.

2) Google's Gemini 4 Carbon has taken first place in the overall ranking. This is a surprise. Lowest hallucination rate, highest intelligence, basically the best model. The exciting part: Initially, it was a race between OpenAI and Anthropic. Then SpaceXSI re-entered the fray with Grok. Then Meta came along with Muse Wunderful, and now Google is suddenly back as well. What started as a two-horse race has become a five-horse race. Everything is wide open again, and the moat seems to be shrinking. Extremely exciting and surprising!

今天是个很有趣的一天。 有两件事很突出:

我发现很多程序员，包括我自己在内，其实特别容易陷入一种技术自嗨。

今天研究一个新的 Agent 框架，明天研究 RAG，后天又去折腾 Skill、MCP、各种自动化工作流。每天都在 GitHub 上看项目，都在研究最新的模型，感觉自己学到了很多东西，技术能力也确实在进步，但你要问这些东西到底解决了谁的问题，有没有真实用户，有没有人愿意付费，很多时候自己都说不明白。

尤其是现在 AI 编程越来越强，很多以前需要花不少时间才能开发的功能，现在借助 Codex 就能很快搭出来。一个人做个网站、做个 Agent、做套自动化系统，门槛确实比以前低了不少。

但问题来了，当越来越多人都有能力做出类似的产品时，你凭什么认为自己的东西就有人买？技术实现只是一个环节，真正困难的可能是找到需求、建立信任、控制成本，以及让客户持续获得价值。

我现在在企业里做 AI 落地，接触过 GEO、RAG、Agent 和 AI 视频生成之后，对这一点感触越来越深。比如一个数字人视频生成项目，API 已经调通了，视频也成功生成了，从程序员的角度来看，这似乎已经完成了。

但如果客户要求的字幕、包装、画面质量都没有达到标准，这个项目实际上还是没法交付。你不能跟客户说我的接口返回成功了，所以你应该满意。人家买的不是一个成功的 HTTP 响应，而是一个真正能解决业务问题的结果。

技术人真的应该多学一点商业、产品、用户心理和沟通。你能写出代码，是技术能力；你能让别人愿意使用，是产品能力；你能找到客户、理解需求、完成交付并获得收入，那才是真正的商业能力。

而且我觉得最可怕的不是你技术不够强，而是你花了很多年把技术练得特别厉害，却从来没有认真研究过自己的能力到底怎么创造价值。

技术当然要学深，但千万别把技术本身当成了最终目的。

posts.text:
It’s pretty wild how frontier LLMs have crossed the chasm on inverse graphics. 

Young founders will start decompiling reality, building RL environments, and print money doing it. Incumbents won't be too happy unless they're fast to adapt.

Case in point -- I gave AI a 3D scan of my parents old house, and it rebuilt the room in Blender. Then I turned off the gravity.

Here’s how it works:

1. ~400 photos I took in 2019 go through RealityScan and become a photogrammetry mesh
2. GPT-6 Astra rebuilds it as a clean, editable Blender scene, using the scan as reference
3. Scan textures become procedural materials. No downloaded assets
4. Every object is isolated and editable, so the physics just works

Turning messy scans into scenes modeled the way an artist would used to take days of skilled work. Huge implications for VFX, AR/VR and robotics.

最近A股行情很不好，心情复杂，最近最大的一个感触是：我们这代股民最大的误解，是误以为国运等于股价。

《经济学人》最新一期文章也说中国股市是个罕见例外，提出了一个非常扎心刺骨的灵魂拷问：
“如果这个国家正在赢得未来，那为什么它的股市投资者们却如此沮丧？”

咱们很多人看宏观叙事，总习惯把“产业打赢了”直接等同于“投资赚到钱了”。

过去几年，新能源、光伏、动力电池、智能硬件、AI 开源，无论从产能规模、出海速度还是技术迭代来看，中国产业链在全球都打出了堪称恐怖的统治力。

但在二级市场的 K 线图上，全球主要股市都在轮番刷出历史新高，唯独这里的股票市场成了一个全球罕见的痛苦例外。

这种反差撕开的，是所有股民和创业者必须补上的一堂硬核金融常识：
国家的产业竞争力，和股民的资本回报率（ROE），在底层从来不是同一套账本。

西方资本市场的底层设计，是一台极致偏向股东回报的提款机。

美股科技巨头哪怕赚了钱，也要把大笔现金拿去回购注销股票、分红给二级市场，优先维持高净资产收益率和股价泡沫，

它们追求的是维持高利润率、筑高专利墙，用资本溢价去奖励持股的人。

而中国产业叙事的底层逻辑，是一台把全要素生产率推向极致的“工业扩张机器”。

任何一个行业一旦被证明有前景，海量的产业资本、地方政策和创业团队就会瞬间涌入；
大家拼的不是谁给股东多分红，而是谁能以最快的速度把成本打穿、把价格卷到极限，把全球竞争对手直接挤出市场。

这种极致的性价比和产能过剩，给国家赢得了全球市场份额，给消费者赢得了极致便宜的商品，但唯独留给上市公司本身的，是薄如刀片的利润率和永无止境的资本开支。

股市在不同体系里的使命从第一天起就截然相反：
一个是拿来给居民沉淀财富、享受资本复利的资产池，
另一个在很大程度上，是承担为实体经济输血、分担创新风险、以低成本进行产业重资产融资的资本工具。

当你把辛苦积攒的积蓄投进去，你以为自己是在分享产业升级的红利，
实际上你的每一分钱，都在作为高强度的研发耗材和产能补贴，被无声砸进了重构全球工业版图的超级熔炉里。

看懂了这个巨大的结构性错位，你才会明白那种沮丧到底从何而来：
世界正在被中国制造重塑，但制造奇迹的功臣们，却不得不承受资本市场上最漫长的一场脱钩。

国家的产业竞争力，和股民的资本回报率（ROE），在底层从来不是同一套账本。

西方资本市场的底层设计，是一台极致偏向股东回报的提款机。

美股科技巨头哪怕赚了钱，也要把大笔现金拿去回购注销股票、分红给二级市场，优先维持高净资产收益率和股价泡沫，

它们追求的是维持高利润率、筑高专利墙，用资本溢价去奖励持股的人。

而中国产业叙事的底层逻辑，是一台把全要素生产率推向极致的“工业扩张机器”。

任何一个行业一旦被证明有前景，海量的产业资本、地方政策和创业团队就会瞬间涌入；
大家拼的不是谁给股东多分红，而是谁能以最快的速度把成本打穿、把价格卷到极限，把全球竞争对手直接挤出市场。

这种极致的性价比和产能过剩，给国家赢得了全球市场份额，给消费者赢得了极致便宜的商品，但唯独留给上市公司本身的，是薄如刀片的利润率和永无止境的资本开支。

股市在不同体系里的使命从第一天起就截然相反：
一个是拿来给居民沉淀财富、享受资本复利的资产池，
另一个在很大程度上，是承担为实体经济输血、分担创新风险、以低成本进行产业重资产融资的资本工具。

当你把辛苦积攒的积蓄投进去，你以为自己是在分享产业升级的红利，
实际上你的每一分钱，都在作为高强度的研发耗材和产能补贴，被无声砸进了重构全球工业版图的超级熔炉里。

看懂了这个巨大的结构性错位，你才会明白那种沮丧到底从何而来：
世界正在被中国制造重塑，但制造奇迹的功臣们，却不得不承受资本市场上最漫长的一场脱钩。

posts.text:
白天刚在法庭上输掉与 OpenAI 的百亿对决，当晚马斯克坐在福布斯晚宴上，状态失神的让人心疼，但他却说出了全场最让人脊背发凉的一句话：
AI 在全方位超越人类，大概只剩一两年，连创新这种人类最后的自尊，马上也要被彻底端平了。

马斯克这个大帅比真的牛逼，在输掉了一场关乎全球最大 AI 资产控制权的官司之后，他没有把时间浪费在抱怨法官或对手身上，而是用一种罕见的失神状态讲出了这番话：

“我对 AI 既惊恐又兴奋，AI 在各方面超越人类，大概不出一两年。”

很多人看热闹，总以为这只是一次商业巨头败诉后的公关失态，或者又一次习惯性的技术恐吓。

但如果我们把败诉这个残酷的现实切口拼上去，就会发现这其实是一个顶级操盘手在亲手被踢下棋盘后，吐出的一句绝望真话：
当创造者自己都被商业机制和法律条文剥夺了对 AI 舵盘的掌控权时，连世界首富也不得不面对现实——
人类这个物种，正在以天为单位，快速滑向丧失全面主导权的边缘。

在过去的认知里，人类总喜欢把最后一张自尊的底牌压在“创新”和“灵性”上。

大家觉得算力再强也只能模仿套路，机器只能消化人类喂给它的旧数据，真正的逻辑跃迁、底层发明和灵光一闪，永远属于肉身大脑。

但在专访里，马斯克彻底敲碎了这个自欺欺人的遮羞布：
AI 在全方位碾压人类，不仅包含算力、记忆和体力，更包含了人类最引以为傲的“无中生有”的发明与创新能力。

每天都在爆发的算法突破，连站在全球算力最前沿的人都感到头晕目眩。
当创新本身被转化成一种以光速自我演进的高维算法时，肉身科学家的迭代速度，在它面前慢得就像地质纪元里的冰川。

更刺骨的是，面对这种全方位的智力降维打击，马斯克最终收敛成了一句近乎无力的祈祷：
“我希望它对我们友好。”
以前的商业战争，输了可以重组资本、招募团队，在下一个周期杀回来。

但 AI 时代的游戏规则完全变了：
一旦智能的代际差距拉大到无法逾越的断层，人类之间为了权力和控制权而打的每一场官司，在未来那个冷酷的超级智能眼里，都轻得像一群蚂蚁为了面包屑打架。

所以我们别再争论谁在这场官司里赢了名誉和金钱，
当裁判哨声吹响的时候，场上的两位棋手可能都还没意识到：
那个在棋盘深处不断被喂大的造物，已经快要站起身来，把整张桌子掀掉了。

AI 在全方位碾压人类，不仅包含算力、记忆和体力，更包含了人类最引以为傲的“无中生有”的发明与创新能力。

每天都在爆发的算法突破，连站在全球算力最前沿的人都感到头晕目眩。
当创新本身被转化成一种以光速自我演进的高维算法时，肉身科学家的迭代速度，在它面前慢得就像地质纪元里的冰川。

更刺骨的是，面对这种全方位的智力降维打击，马斯克最终收敛成了一句近乎无力的祈祷：
“我希望它对我们友好。”
以前的商业战争，输了可以重组资本、招募团队，在下一个周期杀回来。

但 AI 时代的游戏规则完全变了：
一旦智能的代际差距拉大到无法逾越的断层，人类之间为了权力和控制权而打的每一场官司，在未来那个冷酷的超级智能眼里，都轻得像一群蚂蚁为了面包屑打架。

所以我们别再争论谁在这场官司里赢了名誉和金钱，
当裁判哨声吹响的时候，场上的两位棋手可能都还没意识到：
那个在棋盘深处不断被喂大的造物，已经快要站起身来，把整张桌子掀掉了。

OpenAI 即日起把 ChatGPT Pro 各档和 Business Premium 的用量上限翻倍，原定明天的 Pro 200 降额取消，价格没提变化

Tibo 说，Pro 100、Pro 200、Pro 500 三档和 Business Premium 的所有用量上限翻倍，当天生效。Plus 不在名单里。

【我现在能用多少】

按 OpenAI 此前公布的倍数推算（以 Plus 为 1 倍）：Pro 100 从 5 倍变成 10 倍，Pro 500 从 25 倍变成 50 倍。Business Premium 是 Business 套餐里的高级席位，此前倍数官方没公开，只知道翻倍。

Pro 200 要分两种人看。

9 月 29 日前就订阅的老用户，原本 10 月 30 日起要从 20 倍降到 10 倍，现在不降了，Tibo 说你的 Codex 和 Work 用量“保持不变”，也就是继续 20 倍。

9 月底之后新订阅的用户一直是 10 倍，翻倍后也到 20 倍。

这样算下来，三档 Pro 每花 1 美元能用的量还是一样，买贵的不多送。帖子没提价格调整。

【dot 的额度怎么算】

dot 是 OpenAI 9 月底开发者大会发布的常驻 AI agent，有自己的云端电脑，能在后台长时间替你干活，Pro 和 Business Premium 送第一个。

上线时 OpenAI 给了第一个月的加长额度，dot 的用量和你平时的套餐额度分开算。

按 9 月 29 日上线算，一个月差不多到期，Tibo 说这个加长额度“暂时”继续给，dot 的用量也继续单独计算。“暂时”是多久，他没说。

【我现在能用多少】

按 OpenAI 此前公布的倍数推算（以 Plus 为 1 倍）：Pro 100 从 5 倍变成 10 倍，Pro 500 从 25 倍变成 50 倍。Business Premium 是 Business 套餐里的高级席位，此前倍数官方没公开，只知道翻倍。

9 月底之后新订阅的用户一直是 10 倍，翻倍后也到 20 倍。

dot 是 OpenAI 9 月底开发者大会发布的常驻 AI agent，有自己的云端电脑，能在后台长时间替你干活，Pro 和 Business Premium 送第一个。

Let's take what Sam Altman is saying seriously for a second.

He says the following is within reach:

"Self-replicating data centers, this idea that you can use AI to control robots and run factories and build turbines or solar panels and build data centers. But I think we have that within grasp."

There are currently three major bottlenecks:

- Compute
- Energy
- Human labor

Sam Altman believes this triad of problems will be solved if robots build data centers, solar power or future fusion energy are used to power them, and chip production is simultaneously accelerated. It's certainly unclear whether this is being said to reassure the market and offer a positive outlook. But it would be nothing short of revolutionary if a solution to this triad were within reach, because everything depends on it.

Broccoli (W22) is building an AI front office for home services businesses, answering calls, following up with leads, and booking appointments across voice and text.

Today, they serve more than 500 customers, are booking jobs at a run rate of over $1 billion a year, and expect to end the year at more than $60 million in ARR, up from zero just two years ago, after recently raising a $30 million Series B.  

In this fireside, @call_broccoli's founders @abhishekjain25 and @adityaketkar join YC's @gustaf to share the long path to finding that business, from an earlier EV startup that never found product-market fit to visiting 140 contractors across the Bay Area to understand their biggest problems firsthand. They explain how embedding inside a plumbing company led to the first version of Broccoli, why answering missed calls became the wedge, and how AI could eventually reshape the work of technicians themselves.

top_replies.text: @garrytan Pointing the agent at a doc and letting it set itself up is exactly what non-coders need. Most setup guides assume you live in the terminal.

top_replies.text: @garrytan hosted is the part people underrate. most agent memory setups i've seen stall at "who runs the db", not at retrieval

top_replies.name: wilsonlu
top_replies.text:
@garrytan The underrated part is one brain shared across agents. When Claude Code writes code and another bot runs ops, the pain is neither knows what the other decided.

Point both at the same store with one rule: read before each task, write decisions after. Fixes most handoff mess.

Eugenia Kuyda of @Wabi predicts that within a year, one of the biggest consumer AI platforms will be multiplayer, with real network effects:

"Today most AI products are single player. And I would say that you could probably argue they don't have much of a moat. They don't necessarily have switching costs."

"It was pretty easy to move between, say, Claude and ChatGPT, but at least they had some memory about me. With these single player agents, it's so easy to jump between them because all the context is in my Gmail."

"I think in a year what we'll see is that one of the biggest consumer AI platforms will be multiplayer and will have network effects in it. Right now we just sort of agree that single player is the way to go for most AI products."

"A year from now, I think we'll look back at it as more kind of the early innings, and the products that win  will have a lot of network effects and be focused on you talking to other people, not just AI."

@ekuyda w/ @sophiadew on @MTSLive

a16z's Erin Price-Wright says factory technicians can now retool production lines with AI in 20 minutes, a job that used to take an outside integrator 3 months:

"Historically, if you're setting up a line with a lot of automation, you really need to be producing a lot of one single thing. That's how you get the cost down, and how you justify investing in a pretty bespoke manufacturing line."

"But what we're seeing across our portfolio is that manufacturing technicians themselves have the intuition, and now the software tools, to change the economics of producing low-volume, high-mix on the line."

"A manufacturing technician, not necessarily someone with a college degree or who's studied software engineering, can now use these tools to reprogram and reconfigure their lines on the fly, because they understand the manufacturing process."

"Instead of calling a systems integrator, which takes 3 months and hundreds of thousands of dollars to reconfigure a line, you can have a manufacturing engineer use Claude and do that in 20 minutes. That's been a real game changer."

@espricewright

a16z's Connor Love says building for defense is how America builds for everything else, because once you can make the parts "to quality and to cost," new markets start to make sense:

"When you build many systems, you also require many subsystems below that. There are really interesting military systems being built today. The corollary: by building towards defense, you also build for a different industry."

"The subsystems that go into some of our military systems are the exact same subsystems that are going to go into the future robotic systems. It's the actuators, the motors, the valves and switches."

"When you can build those to quality and to cost, then all of a sudden other markets that maybe weren't viable make sense... You're going to have this robotic wave that will come in America."

"AI can't turn a wrench yet. They will eventually. And that will be enabled by all that, actuators and switches and subsystems that we built... And we're not going to have to rely on factories in China."

"As you build an industrial base, an industrial base can be used for many things. Down to the component level, I just think we don’t have enough of it in America."

@ConnorLoveCA @espricewright @VirtualElena
